- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., 1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to reflect bearish sentiment’s reversal potential.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — leading to overcorrection; dampen forecast slope after sharp moves.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: model often fails to capture gradual pullback after peaks; apply slight downward bias in mid-to-late forecast horizon.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5–7 days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast early to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Forecasts with high sentiment volatility (alternating +1/-1) show higher error; use smoother trend filters or reduce volatility-weighted adjustments.
